newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rate hike prompted by guilder-mark weakness - DNB.
newsitem.headline: Rate hike prompted by guilder-mark weakness - DNB.

text.p: Guilder-weakness against the mark prompted the Dutch central bank to raise its rate on short-term liquidity by 10 basis points to 3.00 percent on Thursday, a central bank spokesman said.
The 10 basis points hike brings the rate on special advances to three percent, in line with the German repo rate.
"We find the current mark rate compared to the guilder very high and this was the reason to raise the advances," the central bank spokesman said.
The guilder was quoted at 112.60 per 100 marks before the Dutch central bank raised the special advances.
By 1425 GMT it was quoted at 112.585 per 100 marks.
Asked if the current rate hike would be followed by another move in the short-term was not answered as the Dutch central bank "does not give any predictions".
The special advances rate sets the tone for money market rates.
Dealers were somewhat surprised about the move but said it would not make a big difference for money market rates as call money had been lingering near 3.00 percent for some time.
"And the effect on depossits will be negligible," said one dealer.
The Dutch central bank said the move was not promped by the fact that the German equivalent, the repo, had been fixed at 3.00 for some time.
Earlier today the Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged and kept the repo at a fixed 3.00 percent.
